caption: Fig. 1: Model Illustration. A Deep Convolutional Neural Network such as VGG-16 or ResNet-101 is employed in a fully convolutional fashion, using atrous convolution to reduce the degree of signal downsampling (from 32x down 8x). A bilinear interpolation stage enlarges the feature maps to the original image resolution. A fully connected CRF is then applied to refine the segmentation result and better capture the object boundaries.
description:

It shows the input image, the DCNN with atrous convolution, the aeroplane coarse score map, the final output, the fully connected CRF, and the bi-linear interpolation.

caption: Fig. 2: Illustration of atrous convolution in 1-D. (a) Sparse feature extraction with standard convolution on a low resolution input feature map. (b) Dense feature extraction with atrous convolution with rate r = 2 , applied on a high resolution input feature map.
description:

The figure consists of two main parts: (a) standard convolution on a low-resolution input feature map, and (b) atrous convolution with a rate of 2 on a high-resolution input feature map.

caption: Fig. 4: Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP). To classify the center pixel (orange), ASPP exploits multi-scale features by employing multiple parallel filters with different rates. The effective Field-Of-Views are shown in different colors.
description:
Section 1: Figure showing Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) in DeepLab for semantic image segmentation. It illustrates how ASPP uses multiple parallel filters with different rates to classify the center pixel in an input feature map. Each filter has a different rate, resulting in varying effective field-of-views, depicted in different colors.

Section 2: Four parallel convolutional filters with 3x3 kernels and rates of 6, 12, 18, and 24. The input feature map is processed by these filters to produce multi-scale features, which are then pooled to classify the center pixel. The figure shows the effective field-of-views of each filter.

caption: Fig. 5: Score map (input before softmax function) and belief map (output of softmax function) for Aeroplane. We show the score (1st row) and belief (2nd row) maps after each mean field iteration. The output of last DCNN layer is used as input to the mean field inference.
description:

caption: Fig. 9: DeepLab results based on VGG-16 net or ResNet101 before and after CRF. The CRF is critical for accurate prediction along object boundaries with VGG-16, whereas ResNet-101 has acceptable performance even before CRF.
description:
Figure Description: This figure displays a comparison of semantic image segmentation results using different neural network architectures and the application of Conditional Random Fields (CRF). It shows two images of cyclists and motorcyclists, each segmented using VGG-16 and ResNet101 networks, both before and after applying CRF. The segmentations are visualized with different colors overlaying the original images.

Text in Figure: Image, VGG-16 Bef., VGG-16 Aft., ResNet Bef., ResNet Aft.

Section 1: Figure shows segmentation results of cyclists and motorcyclists using VGG-16 and ResNet101 networks, both before and after applying CRF. The CRF significantly improves boundary accuracy for VGG-16, while ResNet101 shows acceptable performance even without CRF.

Section 2: VGG-16 Bef., VGG-16 Aft., ResNet Bef., ResNet Aft. show segmentations of cyclists and motorcyclists. VGG-16 benefits greatly from CRF, while ResNet101 performs well without it.
